prompt:
Analyze the following external review that has been addressed.
Identify what our INTERNAL code review should have caught
BEFORE the external reviewer found it.

## External Review Feedback


## Code Comments (with Resolutions)
- [operators/keystone/internal/controller/keystone_controller_test.go:3290] Remove lines 3287-3290. We have no interest in testing the value of constants we declare ourselves. There is no good reason to test if `KeystoneSecretNameIndexKey` has the value we assign to it.

## Resolution Summary
Removed the `g.Expect(KeystoneSecretNameIndexKey).To(Equal("spec.secretRefs.name"), ...)` assertion (and its preceding explanatory comment) from `TestKeystoneSecretIndexerKey_IsDeclaredAsConst` in `keystone_controller_test.go`, per the reviewer's point that testing a self-declared constant's value has no value. The test's doc comment was also reworded to drop the 'documented value' framing and instead describe what the test actually verifies now — that `registerSecretNameIndex` passes the `KeystoneSecretNameIndexKey` constant to `IndexField`, ensuring registration and lookup sites share one source of truth.

Extract 0-3 review improvement patterns. For each:
- name: Short, action-oriented name IN ENGLISH
- review_area: error-handling | security | testing | performance | type-safety | validation | architecture | naming | documentation
- detection_hint: How should the reviewer detect this?
- severity: BLOCKING | WARNING
- what_to_check: What exactly to check
- why_it_matters: Why it matters
- example_feedback: Original quote from the reviewer
- example_fix: What was changed

QUALITY: Only real review blindspots. No subjective style opinions.
Nothing that only a domain expert could know.
If nothing extractable: empty array.

LANGUAGE: ALL fields MUST be in English.

Response: ONLY JSON array.
